ticket.title: a contract change compiles in its own repo and breaks consumers in two others, and no gate builds across repositories
ticket.description: Measured 2026-11-10, and it has already cost ten tickets. SP-41 added three optional fields to VerificationReceipt in gaugeblock-contracts. Every storypole gate ran green, because storypole own workspace compiled. Two consumers construct that type literally and do not spread defaults: joiner-core src/engine/mod.rs and benchwork-core tests/archive_service_tests.rs. Both stopped compiling the moment the contract landed. Nothing reported it - no chain builds across repositories, and miter contracts checks schema drift rather than compilation - so the breakage sat in main until an unrelated storypole verification happened to pull joiner-core into its build, and then benchwork into another. Two fix commits later (joiner a301233, benchwork de8ad04) main compiles again. OF-41 is the sibling gate and deliberately does not cover this: it resolves every member from outside the suite with cargo metadata, which answers published-crates-only, and it never compiles. Wanted: a cross-repository build check - each member compiled against the workspace as checked out, in one pass, failing with the crate and the diagnostic - run at the atomic-commit gate for any change to a shared contract crate. Acceptance: reverting SP-41 contract change makes the gate fail naming joiner-core and benchwork-core, restoring it makes the gate pass, and a change confined to one repository does not pay for the whole fleet.

Measured 2026-11-10, and it has already cost ten tickets. SP-41 added three optional fields to VerificationReceipt in gaugeblock-contracts. Every storypole gate ran green, because storypole own workspace compiled. Two consumers construct that type literally and do not spread defaults: joiner-core src/engine/mod.rs and benchwork-core tests/archive_service_tests.rs. Both stopped compiling the moment the contract landed. Nothing reported it - no chain builds across repositories, and miter contracts checks schema drift rather than compilation - so the breakage sat in main until an unrelated storypole verification happened to pull joiner-core into its build, and then benchwork into another. Two fix commits later (joiner a301233, benchwork de8ad04) main compiles again. OF-41 is the sibling gate and deliberately does not cover this: it resolves every member from outside the suite with cargo metadata, which answers published-crates-only, and it never compiles. Wanted: a cross-repository build check - each member compiled against the workspace as checked out, in one pass, failing with the crate and the diagnostic - run at the atomic-commit gate for any change to a shared contract crate. Acceptance: reverting SP-41 contract change makes the gate fail naming joiner-core and benchwork-core, restoring it makes the gate pass, and a change confined to one repository does not pay for the whole fleet.

DONE 2026-11-10 (outfeed 33409fb). `outfeed consumers <suite-root>` compiles every member with cargo check --manifest-path from the suite root, so the harness config applies - deliberately the opposite of `outfeed standalone`, which resolves from outside to prove the published ecosystem. Failures name the member and the first short-format diagnostic. 101 tests in outfeed-core + outfeed-orchestrator, fmt clean, clippy -D warnings exit 0. THE GATE IMMEDIATELY FOUND A THIRD CONSUMER: outfeed-orchestrator src/backlog.rs constructs VerificationReceipt literally and has not compiled since SP-41 - in the same repository, invisible for the same reason as the other two, because nothing here builds a crate it does not own. Fixed with diff/diff_hash/window_intact = None: outfeed apply certifies a release and never examined a window, so window_intact=true would have been a receipt asserting something it did not check. MEASURED, and it changes where this belongs: one full pass took 11.0 min warm for all 11 members (darwin, stable, sequential; log timestamps, not a stopwatch). Per-member checks churn feature unification, so shared dependencies re-check per repository - the marginal member is not cheap. That makes this a contract-change gate, not an inner-loop one, and scoping it to the dependents of changed crates is the follow-up rather than a nice-to-have. ALSO FIXED while watching it: the first live run printed nothing for eleven minutes because the report was assembled before being printed; check_consumers_with streams per member to stderr so --json on stdout stays machine-readable. NOTE: the installed binary predates that streaming change, so the next `outfeed install` is what carries it.
